title: Consumption Safety Net: QBR Usage & Billing Scenarios (worksheet draft)
body:
Purpose:
A working worksheet to walk through customer-specific consumption scenarios for QBRs. Focus: rapid identification of billing & token-risk, automated alerting thresholds, and recommended remediation paths that can be proposed during renewal conversations. Draft — has open questions and calculation checks.

Quick summary (one-liner):
Capture current consumption profile, simulate 3 shock scenarios, set pragmatic alert thresholds, and propose 1–3 remediation runbooks to reduce budget/surge risk before renewal.

How to use this sheet during QBR prep:
- Populate the left column with actuals from billing and usage exports (last 90 days preferred).
- Run the scenario rows (A/B/C) to show high/medium/low probability spikes.
- Use the escalation matrix to recommend immediate and long-term actions (rate limits, burst caps, dedicated capacity).
- Capture owner + timeline for each action item in the final section to carry forward to renewal negotiation.

Sections (worksheet layout):
1) Customer metadata (manual fill)
- Account name: ______
- ARR band: ______
- Primary contact: ______
- Region(s): ______
- Plan type: Hosted / Dedicated / Private
- Billing cadence: Monthly / Quarterly / Annual

2) Last 90 days actuals (paste from export) — key fields to pull: date, tokens_in, tokens_out, peak_rps, average_latency_ms, cost_usd, route/path
- NOTE: verify tokens_in/out mapping to model ops (e.g., chat vs embed)

3) Baseline metrics (derived) — fill these from the export or instrumented dashboard:
- 90d avg tokens/day: ______
- 90d p95 tokens/day: ______
- 90d peak RPS: ______
- Average cost per 1k tokens (observed): $____
- Percent usage on low-cost model variants (quantized): ____%

4) Scenario simulations (example rows to copy into presentation)
Columns: scenario_name | multiplier | expected_peak_rps | estimated_daily_tokens | estimated_daily_cost_usd | notes
Rows (examples):
- Baseline Stable | 1.0 | (use p95) | calc: avg_tokens * 1.0 | calc: tokens*$/1k | typical day
- Burst Spike - marketing campaign | 3.5 | ~peak*3.5 | avg_tokens*3.5 | show cost delta and time-to-breach | short 48–72h spike
- Slow Growth + Rollout | 1.6 | ~peak*1.6 | avg_tokens*1.6 | moderate sustained increase — renewal risk
- Regression / Model Drift | 2.0 | increased tokenization (longer outputs) | tokens*2.0 | potential quality remediation cost

(Quick calc snippet for presenter):
estimated_daily_cost_usd = estimated_daily_tokens / 1000 * observed_cost_per_1k_tokens
show delta_vs_baseline = estimated_daily_cost_usd - baseline_daily_cost_usd

5) Rate-limits & budget-alert templates (for product ops / infra handoff)
- Immediate alert thresholds (email + Slack):
  - Alert A (notice): when daily spend > baseline_daily_spend * 1.25 OR rolling 1h tokens > p95*1.5
  - Alert B (high): when daily spend > baseline_daily_spend * 1.6 OR rolling 10m tokens > peak_rps*2.0
  - Alert C (critical): when projected 7-day spend > committed_budget OR observed sustained RPS > peak_rps*3 for >30m
- Recommended alert payloads: customer_id, account_owner, estimated_spend_delta, top_routes_by_tokens, sample_requests (redacted), last_successful_model_version

6) Budget escape hatch / automated actions (operational knobs)
- Soft throttle: apply per-route soft-rate-limit that returns 429+Retry-After; recommended when Alert B triggered
- Graceful fallback: route to lower-cost quantized model variant (same output format) when sustained 5m avg token rate > threshold
- Pre-emptive caching: enable prefix caching for deterministic prompts when Alert A triggers (training prompt whitelist required)
- Emergency cutover: switch to Dedicated reserved capacity with pre-approved budget bump (requires sales/finance signoff)

7) Escalation matrix (who to call, example messages):
- Tier 1: Customer Success (owner) — initial outreach + triage (template below)
- Tier 2: Solutions Eng — implement throttles/fallbacks + quick config changes
- Tier 3: Platform Ops / SRE — if infrastructure scaling or capacity migration required
- Finance/Sales: confirm budget/commit changes (if >20% projected increase)

Outreach template (CS -> customer, short):
Subject: "Usage spike detected — proposed short-term mitigation"
Hi <Name>,
We observed a significant increase in token usage on <route> starting <time>. Our recommended short-term action is to enable a soft throttle and route non-critical traffic to a lower-cost model for the next 48 hours. Estimated cost impact avoided: ~$X. Can we schedule a 20m quick sync now?
Best,
<Maya / CS owner>

8) Renewal playbook notes (how to fold into QBR):
- Bring scenario deltas (baseline vs 3 scenarios) + recommended escalation path as a 1-slide summary
- Propose 2 renewal options: (a) baseline extension with budget guard rails + alerting + 90-day review; (b) committed reserved capacity (discounted) + migration plan + 30-day SLA improvement
- Attach runbook (section 6) and assign owners before renewal meeting

9) Example action-item tracker (copy to repo)
- Action: Enable per-route soft throttle for /chat-v1 | Owner: Priya | ETA: 2026-03-05 | Status: TBD
- Action: Evaluate quantized model for FAQ route | Owner: Lena | ETA: 2026-03-12 | Status: testing
- Action: Finance confirm emergency commit threshold | Owner: Ethan | ETA: 2026-03-07 | Status: in_progress

10) Open questions / TODOs (draft notes to self)
- Need to standardize "observed_cost_per_1k_tokens" calculation across hosts (artifact: billing-export-v2).
- Confirm whether we can programmatically surface sample requests (privacy/legal check).
- Should we auto-suggest model-fallback mapping per-route? (idea: ML-driven mapping based on content-type)
- Presentation: include 1-sentence explainer for non-technical execs on why tokenization length can grow after model changes.

Appendix: quick sample numbers (fill with customer-specific actuals during prep)
- baseline_daily_tokens: 1,200,000 tokens/day
- observed_cost_per_1k_tokens: $0.39 / 1k tokens
- baseline_daily_cost_usd = 1,200,000 / 1000 * 0.39 = $468.00
- Burst Spike (x3.5) -> tokens/day = 4,200,000 -> est cost = $1,638 -> delta = $1,170/day

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the worksheet compact — execs want 1 slide + backup.
- Add a short 'what we changed' row when recommending model fallback so customer sees quality trade-offs documented.
- For Dedicated customers, include a simple capacity migration checklist and expected time (24–72h depending on region).

End of draft worksheet.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-17: initial sketch (Maya)
- 2025-12-09: added alert templates and calc snippets (Ethan)
- 2026-02-28: updated remediation options and appendix numbers (Priya)
